items.name: Earthsong Gardens
items.summary: A regenerative growing community restoring soil and pollinators. We swap heirloom seeds, share harvests, and govern the land together through liquid democracy.

items.name: Seed Keepers Alliance
items.summary: Guardians of heirloom seed diversity. Members save, label and swap seeds so no variety is lost.

items.name: Pollinator Corridor
items.summary: A ribbon of wildflower meadows linking gardens across the valley so bees and butterflies can travel safely. Planted and tended by volunteers.

items.name: Community Tool Library
items.summary: A free lending library of power tools, garden equipment and know-how. Borrow what you need, return it cared-for, teach the next person.

items.name: Hands needed for Saturday fence rebuild
items.summary: The community garden fence came down in the storm. Looking for a few neighbours to help rebuild it this Saturday — lunch is on the garden.

card.because: A monoculture requires constant defence. A diverse system defends itself. The garden that thrives with least intervention is the garden that works with nature, not against it.
card.care_about: Designing growing spaces where the cultivated and the wild support each other — not a garden that holds nature at bay but one that invites it in.
card.drift_looks_like: Aesthetics that eliminate wildness. Neatness as a value that crowds out biodiversity.
card.in_conflict: The insect over the weed-free path.
looks_like: Leaving areas deliberately unmown and uncultivated
Planting for pollinators and birds as deliberately as planting for the table
card.never_do: Remove a plant without first asking what depends on it.
